uvant.explanation: "Uvant" means "unfamiliar". It is built from "u-" (not) and "vant" (used to). To say what you are not used to, add "med" (with): "Jeg er uvant med kulden" (I am not used to the cold).

uvedkommende.explanation: "Uvedkommende" means "unauthorized". When you say a question has nothing to do with the matter, it means "irrelevant": "et uvedkommende spørgsmål" (an irrelevant question). To keep people out of a place, a sign says: "Adgang forbudt for uvedkommende" (No entry for unauthorized persons).

uvenlig.explanation: "Uvenlig" means "unfriendly". It is built from "u-" (not) and "venlig" (friendly). To name the person who receives the unfriendly behavior, add "mod" (toward): "Hun var uvenlig mod mig" (She was unfriendly to me).

uventet.explanation: "Uventet" means "unexpected". To say something came as a surprise, put it after the verb: "Det kom helt uventet" (It came completely unexpectedly).

uvidende.explanation: "Uvidende" means "unaware". It is built from "u-" (not) and "at vide" (to know). To name the subject you know nothing about, add "om" (about): "Jeg er uvidende om reglerne" (I am unaware of the rules).

uvidenhed.explanation: "En uvidenhed" means "ignorance". It is the noun for the adjective "uvidende" (unaware). To name the subject you know nothing about, add "om" (about): "uvidenhed om reglerne" (ignorance of the rules).

uærlig.explanation: "Uærlig" means "dishonest". It is built from "u-" (not) and "ærlig" (honest).

at vaccinere.explanation: "At vaccinere" means "to vaccinate". To name the disease, add "mod" (against): "vaccinere mod influenza" (vaccinate against the flu). To say you are the person getting the shot, use "at lade sig vaccinere" (to let yourself be vaccinated): "Jeg lader mig vaccinere" (I am getting vaccinated).

at vade.explanation: "At vade" means "to wade". To say you walk out into the sea, add "ud i" (out into): "Vi vader ud i havet" (We wade out into the sea). To say someone is very rich, use "i penge" (in money): "Hun vader i penge" (She is rolling in money).

at vakle.explanation: "At vakle" means "to wobble / waver". To say a tired person walks unsteadily, use it for "to wobble": "Han vakler hjem" (He wobbles home). To say a decision is not firm, use it for "to waver": "Hans beslutning vakler" (His decision is wavering).

at vande.explanation: "At vande" means "to water". It comes from "vand" (water). To say you give animals water to drink, use it for them too: "at vande hestene" (to water the horses).

at vandre.explanation: "At vandre" means "to wander / hike". To say you go on foot for a long time in nature, use it for "to hike": "Vi vandrer langs kysten" (We hike along the coast). To say you walk around without hurry or goal, use it for "to wander": "Han vandrede rundt i byen" (He wandered around town).

at vare.explanation: "At vare" means "to last". To say how long something goes on, add the length of time: "Filmen varer to timer" (The movie lasts two hours).

at variere.explanation: "At variere" means "to vary". To say something is not always the same, use it alone: "Prisen varierer" (The price varies). To say you change something on purpose, name the thing after it: "Jeg varierer menuen" (I vary the menu).

at vaske.explanation: "At vaske" means "to wash". To say you wash an object, name it after the verb: "Jeg vasker bilen" (I wash the car). To say you wash yourself, use "at vaske sig" (to wash oneself): "Jeg vasker mig" (I wash myself). To say you do the dishes, use "at vaske op" (to do the dishes): "Hvem vasker op i dag?" (Who is doing the dishes today?)

at vaske gulv.explanation: "At vaske gulv" means "to mop the floor". In this phrase, "gulv" has no article: "Vi vasker gulv om lørdagen" (We mop the floor on Saturdays). To wipe up one spill, use "at tørre op" (to wipe up): "Jeg tørrer mælken op" (I wipe up the milk).

at vaske op.explanation: "At vaske op" means "to do the dishes". To ask whose turn it is, say: "Hvem vasker op i dag?" (Who is doing the dishes today?) Do not mix it up with "at vaske" (to wash). To say you wash a car, say: "Jeg vasker bilen" (I wash the car).

at vaske sig.explanation: "At vaske sig" means "to wash (oneself)". When you talk about another person, "sig" stays the same: "Han vasker sig" (He washes himself). To wash something else, use "at vaske" (to wash) and name the thing: "Jeg vasker bilen" (I wash the car).

at vaske tøj.explanation: "At vaske tøj" means "to do laundry". Literally, it is "to wash clothes". To say you do the dishes, use "at vaske op" (to do the dishes): "Jeg vasker op" (I do the dishes).

at vedkende sig.explanation: "At vedkende sig" means "to acknowledge". The word "sig" always goes with it. To name what you acknowledge, put it after "sig": "Han vedkender sig sin fejl" (He acknowledges his mistake).

at vedligeholde.explanation: "At vedligeholde" means "to maintain". To say you keep a house in good shape, say: "Vi vedligeholder huset" (We maintain the house). To say someone claims something, use "at hævde" (to claim): "Hun hævder, at det er sandt" (She claims that it is true).

at vedlægge.explanation: "At vedlægge" means "to enclose". It is built from "ved" (by) and "at lægge" (to put). To say you put a document in with an email, name it after the verb: "Jeg vedlægger kvitteringen" (I enclose the receipt).

at vedrøre.explanation: "At vedrøre" means "to concern". To say a matter affects someone, put the person after the verb: "Sagen vedrører dig" (The matter concerns you). To start the subject of an email, use "Vedrørende" (Regarding), a form of this word: "Vedrørende din ansøgning" (Regarding your application).

at vedtage.explanation: "At vedtage" means "to pass (a law) / adopt". "Folketinget" is the Danish parliament. To say it made a law official, say: "Folketinget vedtog loven" (Parliament passed the law).

at veje.explanation: "At veje" means "to weigh". To say how heavy you are, use the verb with a number: "Jeg vejer 70 kilo" (I weigh 70 kilos). To weigh an object on a scale, name the object after the verb: "Jeg vejer pakken" (I weigh the package).
